300.title: Airwallex Screen Ritual
300.problem: How to run every coding screen

sections.title: Clarify first
body: Restate the problem in one or two sentences out loud.
Ask: input size, sorted?, duplicates, empty input, same index twice?, no-solution contract, output order.
For strings: character set and case sensitivity.

sections.title: Naive approach
body: Always state a correct brute force first — even if you never type it.
Example: nested loops O(n²) for pair problems.
Airwallex wants progression: trivial → improve.

sections.title: Improve
body: Name the data structure: HashMap, two pointers, sliding window, stack, heap.
Say why it wins on time or space.
Then code with full-word names while narrating.

sections.title: Edges & complexity
body: Universal edges: empty, single element, all equal, negatives/zeros, max n.
End with time + auxiliary space (not just 'input size').
If stuck: name approach A vs B and ask which direction is more productive.

sections.title: Live rules
body: No AI tools in live real-time interviews unless they explicitly allow it.
Prep with AI is fine; the screen is unassisted thinking.
Target: medium comfort in ~30–40 minutes.

sections.title: Say it back
body: Clarify → naive → optimize → example → code → edges → complexity.
Open the tutor app after listening and drill options cold.

301.title: Two Sum
301.problem: Return indices of two numbers that sum to target

sections.title: Clarify
body: Exactly one solution guaranteed?
Distinct indices only (no using the same element twice)?
Negatives / zeros / duplicates allowed?
Must return indices (not values)? May I mutate the array?

sections.title: Naive
body: For each i, for each j > i: if nums[i] + nums[j] == target, return [i, j].
Time O(n²), extra space O(1).
Say this first in the interview even if you skip typing it.

sections.title: Optimal — HashMap
body: Map value → index of numbers already seen.
For each i with value x: complement = target − x.
If complement is in the map, return [map[complement], i].
Else store map[x] = i.
Critical: look up complement BEFORE insert so a single value cannot pair with itself.

sections.title: Walkthrough
body: i=0, x=2 → need 7, miss → store {2:0}.
i=1, x=7 → need 2, hit at 0 → return [0, 1].
Done; later elements unused.

sections.title: Edges & traps
body: [3, 3], target 6 → first stores 3@0; second finds complement at 0 → [0, 1].
Do not return values instead of indices.
Do not pair an element with its own index.
If no guaranteed solution, define empty/error return after the loop.

sections.title: Complexity & trade-off
body: Time O(n) expected with hash map.
Auxiliary space O(n) for the map.
If only values needed and sorting is allowed: sort O(n log n) + two pointers O(n), but original indices need (value, index) pairs.

sections.title: Say it back
body: Clarifiers: unique solution, distinct indices, negatives, duplicates.
Naive nested loops O(n²).
Map value→index; lookup before insert.
O(n) time, O(n) space.
Then open tutor: Two Sum deep drill (8 options).

435.title: Approvals: One Decision, One Audit Trail
435.problem: Design an authorized, auditable approval workflow

sections.title: Ask first
body: When does approval take effect?
Can there be only one final decision?
What are the current-permission, audit, RTO, and RPO requirements?

sections.title: Say the flow
body: Authenticated reviewer sends the expected version.
Check current permission; conditionally transition the pending version.
Commit the target change, decision, audit record, and outbox together, then confirm.

sections.title: Recall under pressure
body: Stale reviewer: conflict. Revoked reviewer: deny.
Outbox repairs notification gaps.
RPO zero needs off-region durable commit before success and a fenced single writer.

436.title: Issue Tracker: Immediate Reads, Delayed Search
436.problem: Design issue creation and full-text search with tenant isolation

sections.title: Ask first
body: Which read must be immediate?
How stale may search be?
How current must permissions be?

sections.title: Say the flow
body: Authorize create; commit the issue and search outbox together.
Serve the author's direct GET from authoritative storage.
Index asynchronously; search returns candidates, then current authorization filters content.

sections.title: Recall under pressure
body: Database owns truth; search may lag ten seconds.
Cached IDs never grant access.
Stale edits get version conflicts; index outages do not block issue creation.

437.title: Jira Dashboard: The Acknowledgment Boundary
437.problem: Keep a customer dashboard current from Jira issue updates

sections.title: Ask first
body: Read-only or write-back?
Freshness target and missed-event repair?
Tenant and event scale?

sections.title: Say the flow
body: Authenticate tenant; durably store the inbox event before acknowledging.
A fair worker conditionally applies newer issue state and commits inbox status plus outbox.
Push an invalidation; the browser refetches authoritative data.

sections.title: Recall under pressure
body: Duplicate: unique tenant and event identity.
Out of order: apply only newer source state.
Worker crash: harmless redelivery. Noisy tenant: fair scheduling and backlog-age metric.

438.title: Import Jobs: Fair Queues and Ambiguous Effects
438.problem: Import changes under a shared downstream API quota

sections.title: Ask first
body: What is one job item?
Is the quota global or tenant-scoped?
Does downstream support idempotency or authoritative lookup?

sections.title: Say the flow
body: Authenticate and idempotently accept durable jobs and items.
Schedule fairly by tenant; obtain a shared quota grant and cap concurrency.
Call downstream; record item and job progress.

sections.title: Recall under pressure
body: A 429 delay is a minimum; do not sleep on the worker.
Timeout after create means outcome unknown without a safe retry contract.
If limiter authority is unavailable, pause unsafe calls.
